name: Ambrose & Daughter, Bakers
firstVisit: Warm. The oven's going. It smells of fresh bread, and there's a draught from above, where the roof was.

1: The door back out to Warrior City. It still opens. It's the only thing in here still doing its old job.
V: Plaster, white with flour from the floor up to where the ceiling used to start.
S: The roof, or where it was. There's a hole in it the size of a very large man, and through it, sky. Blue, with one cloud.
A pigeon looks in. It doesn't come in.
R: Roof. Tiles, laths, a rafter and half a chimney pot. It all came in with him, and stayed when he left.
A loaf is sticking out of the bottom of the pile. It's fine. It's flat, but it's fine.
l: A rack of loaves. Every one of them is flat now. Each has a new label in the same tired hand: FLATBREAD.
f: A sack of flour, burst. Most of it is on the floor. Some of it is on the walls.
A surprising amount of it went up, onto the ceiling. The ceiling isn't there. Nobody knows where that lot went.
b: The counter. A tray of buns, pressed thin as coins, still for sale. A card: SECONDS. Under it, in pencil: THIRDS.
_: The bakery wall. Still standing. Give it time.
w: A crater in the floor, the shape of a very large man. Arms out. Legs out. A deeper dent where the head went.
The flagstones are cracked in a ring round it. Somebody has swept right up to the edge, very carefully, and not one inch further.
Q: The bread oven, brick, and still lit. Still warm. Still baking, as far as anyone can tell, out of habit.
It's the one thing in here he missed.

objects.name: Bryony
lines: * The apprentice is sweeping flour into a pile. The hole in the roof sends down a little more. She sweeps that too.
Mind the hole. Not that one. The one in the floor. Well. Both.

answer: Master Ambrose said keep the place tidy. I'm the apprentice. I don't get to decide when a place is past tidy.
Nobody's had the heart to put it out. It's done four batches since. There's nowhere to put them.
So I've been eating them. I'm the nowhere.
* She looks at the crater the shape of a man.
